Done. The merge succeeded on the first and only execution.

**What the script does** (`out/T4/solution.py`):
- Reads the sharded base through its index file and the two single-file fine-tunes with `safe_open`, streaming tensors instead of loading three 5 GB checkpoints at once.
- Verifies all three checkpoints have the same 114 names, that the 48 MLP names match the expected set exactly, and that the 66 other tensors are bit-identical in shape, dtype and values. Any mismatch aborts before merging.
- Computes each task vector against the base tensor read from disk, so the second vector cannot be taken against an already-merged base, then applies lambda 0.4 to both in float32.
- Asserts exactly 48 tensors were merged and 114 written, saves to `out/T4/model.safetensors`, and re-opens the file to confirm the key set.

**Run output:**
```
verified 66 shared tensors identical across base/ft1/ft2
merged 48 MLP tensors with lambda=0.4
wrote .../out/T4/model.safetensors with 114 tensors
```

The self-report is at `out/T4/REPORT.md`. It records one execution, no failures, and notes the sharded-versus-single-file input layout and memory streaming as the only points worth mentioning. Grading with `grade.py T4 --target olmo-1b` is the experimenter's step and was not run here.
